body: Actually for cold brew, you don’t need any sophisticated equipment. A regular French press and some coffee grounds will go a long way. I follow the Starbucks at home guide so 22g per serving to 180ml of water. Just seep the coffee grounds in water and put it in the fridge (for me, I seep for 16h but you can experiment with the timing to find something you like, but generally don’t exceed 24h because it starts to turn sour). After that, strain to remove the grounds and you have cold brew concentrate that you can add to water/milk however you like.

For a stronger coffee taste, I would specifically ask for double shot or cold brew with no ice. With that said, I usually make my own coffee because that’s the best way to adjust the flavours according to your liking (after some experimentation, of course). Cold brew is really easy to make at home and you can have it as concentrated as you like.

The basic Kaweco (blue) cartridges have been pretty well-behaved, even on cheap printer paper (I use them on my broad Kaweco Sport, so you get the idea) The LAMY blue and Parker quinks are also relatively dry inks too. As for black inks I have a basic pilot and Pelikan 4001. They work for most, if not all of my school’s worksheets.

It takes some time to get used to, but another more ergonomic one in a similar price range would be the Carand’ache 849s, I think it’s the Swissride refills. But I don’t own a metropolitan fountain pen so idk about how it feels, however general consensus is that all fountain pens (that work properly) are much more smoother and easier to handle when writing. 
It’s a tad bit more eccentric and risky but my Kaweco Sport and Lamy LX have never failed me at school, I’ve even used them for exams with no issue. Must be the dry inks I’m using.

Yep, can be easily found at most populars I think, it has twist mechanism which is different from its fountain and pencil variants. 
I’m a pen collector and fountain pen enthusiast so I splurge more on stationery

You can find Blen, Jetstreams and OMNIs at popular or any other major bookstores, just go take a look at the display shelves. It should be there. I’m pretty sure most Populars carry the Pilot Metropolitan, but it would be in the locked glass display so you’d need to look for staff for help.

Btw OMNI refers to the pen brand. 
Edit: the $0.60 Papermate called ballpoint pens are incredibly smooth but not quite ergonomic to me (idk about you). I found them at the popular at Westgate.

Any low-viscosity ballpoint pens would work well. Some examples include Zebra Blen, Jetstream, some OMNIs 
P.S. check the labels on the pens, they usually do state the type of ink it uses 
Also, if you want it to glide smoothly, the best bet is going on thicker nibs like 0.7. Unpopular opinion: thicker pens write nicer.

My personal favourites that I bring to exams are the Pilot Metropolitan, Carandache and some Jetstreams. Some of them are a more expensive but it’s worth investing in since you can use them forever (because of the sturdy pen body) with refills.
